machine.caveat: The two matrix arms ran on a shared machine under unrelated Deno, Python and Xcode load, and under markedly asymmetric contention: the on arm's one-minute load had a median of 24.18 over 22 samples, the off arm's 10.24 over 26. The more contended arm is the faster one, so contention does not account for the elapsed-time difference between them; two single samples do not make a latency baseline either way. The alternating repeat subset, which the timing claims rest on, ran later at a median one-minute load of 6.54 over 16 samples, and alternates the arms so that drift falls on both.

repeatSubset.purpose: Five rounds per arm over the all-backlinks cases at 4, 32 and 128 topics, for a timing distribution. The three 512-topic all-backlinks cases are left out: they are 1090 of the matrix's 2799 seconds and show no shape this span does not.
repeatSubset.ordering: Batched: five rounds of the on arm, then five of the off arm. Superseded for the timing claims by `alternatingSubset`, because batching lets drift in machine state over the sitting correlate with the arm, which is the confound the plan's alternating rule removes.
repeatSubset.rawRecords: Not kept. This ordering is superseded by `alternatingSubset` for every claim, so only its derived timings are retained, which is what the two orderings are compared on.

summary.determinism: Every case of the alternating subset produced one distinct set of counters across its five rounds in each arm, and each set equals the matrix arm's counters for the same case.

limitations: The matrix arms' elapsed times are single samples taken on a loaded shared machine and support no latency conclusion. The repeat subset is where the timing claims come from.

The repeat subset was first run batched, five rounds of one arm then five of the other, and re-run alternating. Both are kept; the alternating run is what the timing claims rest on. The two disagree by up to 16% on individual ratios and disagree on whether the 4-topic case separates, which is why the ordering is recorded rather than left to be inferred.

The repeat subset was first run batched, five rounds of one arm then five of the other, at 2303bcc151, and re-run alternating at 2b6d7244b3. The alternating run is what every timing claim rests on. The two differ by up to 16% on individual ratios and disagree about whether the 4-topic case separates, which is why the ordering is recorded rather than left to be inferred. Only the alternating run's raw samples are kept.

Server execution is not measured here. The headless fixture builds its runtime over an emulated storage manager with no memory server, so the serving loop has nothing to construct over; both modes hold serverExecution off.
The all-backlinks workload is a scaling probe rather than normal UI behavior, as the plan says. The per-workload split is what separates its cost from the topic-open workload's.
One trial of one case is not a rate. Every figure here comes from the runs in this file.

The engagement probe used the cf CLI as its client, not a browser, and a source-run toolshed serves no built shell. It establishes that the ON posture constructs and serves; it does not establish that a browser arm runs coherently, which needs a shell built at the same posture.

Every `complete` record in this file carries no `mode` — the 1 per arm under `arms`, the 5 per arm under `alternatingSubset.arms`, and the `complete` field extracted beside each arm. These runs predate the change that labels that record, so the instrument did not write one; the mode is the one named by the `arms` key the record sits under. Every `environment` and `sample` record here does carry its mode, and no run in this file reached a `limit`. The records are left as the instrument wrote them rather than regenerated to match a later version of it.

alternatingSubset.purpose: The same four cases, run on,off,on,off for five rounds, one probe invocation per arm per round, so drift over the sitting falls on both arms rather than correlating with one. This is what the record's timing claims rest on.
alternatingSubset.head: 2b6d7244b3965173c0ada39e223246ee070852eb
alternatingSubset.dirtyTreeNote: Rounds 2 to 5 ran with uncommitted edits in the tree. Those edits reached topics-headless-fixture.ts, which the probe does load, as well as browser benchmark files and documentation, which it does not; the fixture's were comment-only. What establishes that none of it moved a number is that these rounds' counters equal round 1's, taken with a clean tree, and equal the matrix arms'. Alternating also puts any effect they could have had on both arms.
alternatingSubset.orderingEvidence: roundLog carries each invocation's finishing timestamp in the order they ran, so the interleaving is readable from the data rather than asserted.

serverExecutionEngagementProbe.purpose: Whether server execution's ON posture engages at all, since the headless tier's flag had nothing to engage. Two source-run toolsheds on one revision, identical but for EXPERIMENTAL_SERVER_EXECUTION.
serverExecutionEngagementProbe.head: fd9fa9a44b1d04c53cea863e5c46c48692d0da57

activeSpacesDuringSession.note: Read live from /api/health/stats while the cf piece new session was open. The capture in servingLoopAfterDeployingTopics was taken after that session closed, so its activeSpaces gauge reads 0; this observation is not in the captured file. The cumulative counters beside it are.

serverExecutionEngagementProbe.workloadDriven: cf piece new packages/patterns/topics/main.tsx --root packages/patterns, against the ON toolshed
serverExecutionEngagementProbe.finding: The ON toolshed constructed an ExecutorHost and served the deployed board's work: activeSpaces reached 2 while the session was open, and the cumulative counters recorded 10 waves, 2 authored transactions seen and 10 derived commits across two spaces, with no structure-load failures. The OFF toolshed carried no servingLoop block at all. activeSpaces is a gauge and reads 0 once the session closes; the cumulative counters are the durable evidence.
serverExecutionEngagementProbe.notMeasured: The cost of that posture. This establishes engagement only, with the cf CLI as the client rather than a browser.
serverExecutionEngagementProbe.environment: A toolshed-backed deployment driven by the cf CLI: two source-run toolsheds, no compiled binary, no served shell and no browser. This is not the browser benchmark environment, which runs a built toolshed binary serving a baked shell under Chrome; whether that environment runs a coherent ON arm is not established here.
